name: WILLIS LEASE FINANCE

priced.reason: not a repriceable fcff name or no growth supplied

devils_advocate.strongest_counter: That refusing a fifth time on a discount-rate artifact is an abdication, and that the business case is strong and getting stronger: the 97th percentile of 152 Industrials, lease rent revenue +10.3%, maintenance services +73.7%, management and advisory fees up from $6.4M to $17.9M, record quarterly lease rent of $84.4M, assets under management growing, and a cost of debt the filing shows is 5.0% against a model charging 14%. If the discount rate is genuinely seven points too high then the equity is worth a multiple of the price even on a halved cash-flow base, and five sessions of refusal have cost five slots of coverage for no verdict.
devils_advocate.what_would_prove_it: A disclosure splitting maintenance from growth fleet investment — the single input that would make this name modellable — or a cost of equity the schema could accept.
devils_advocate.already_visible: The split is still not disclosed, and this quarter supplies something better than the split: the composition of the earnings. Gains on sale are 70% of income from operations; income from operations fell 12% while revenue rose 18%; and maintenance reserve revenue, which is the closest thing this company has to an annuity, fell 22%. That is a direct answer to 'the business case is strong': the growth in the reported top line is low-margin parts trading and the profit is portfolio churn. It moves my own lean from fair toward rich. But it does NOT license a verdict, because the 2026-09-23 pass on this name already made the mistake available: correcting the capex alone gives +19.4% required growth and reads rich, correcting the WACC alone gives -13.6% and reads cheap, and publishing either is the one-sided answer. With the nine-month figures the capex correction is far LARGER than any prior pass had (net $560M annualised, not $210M), which widens the spread rather than narrowing it.
devils_advocate.unresolved: The maintenance-versus-growth split, still. The RES rule of 2026-10-30 — compare total capex to D&A, and below it treat all capex as sustaining — does not help here because it runs the other way: fleet purchases of roughly $1.12bn annualised are about nine times D&A of $121M, so most of this spend IS growth and the AROC rescue is available in principle. What I cannot establish is the incremental return on it, which is the whole question for a lessor deploying $560M a year net. I also cannot verify the carrying values of a fleet marked in the tightest aftermarket on record.

what_changed: The Q3 10-Q of 2026-11-03 answers the question the last three passes left open and it answers it against the bull case. The 2026-10-02 pass asked whether gains on sale of leased equipment are 'recurring income or portfolio liquidation'. Nine-month gain on sale is $55,449k against income from operations of $79,251k — 70% — and the answer is neither liquidation nor ordinary income: proceeds from sale were $418,016k against purchases of $837,574k, so Willis is buying roughly twice what it sells. It is churning a growing book into a record aftermarket and booking the spread. Three further things are new and all negative. Income from operations FELL 12.1% ($79.3M from $90.2M) while revenue rose 18.3%. Income before income taxes fell 34.3% ($93.8M from $142.8M, the prior year carrying a $42.95M gain on sale of a business). And maintenance reserve revenue — the recurring, high-margin line — fell 22.2%, to $141.3M from $181.7M; the revenue growth is instead spare parts and equipment sales, $141.0M against $54.0M, on which cost of sales was $120.6M, i.e. a roughly 14% gross margin. Also: a Series B preferred was created (item 3.02, 2026-09-22, articles amended 2026-09-30), a $0.15 quarterly dividend and an enlarged repurchase plan were declared 2026-10-30, $13.0M of loss on debt extinguishment was booked in nine months, and $165.8M of notes payable relate to failed sale-leasebacks on eight engines with repurchase options of $14.7-19.3M each exercisable 2031-2034.
consensus_case: The market is paying $993M of equity on top of $2.52bn of debt for an aircraft engine lessor whose reported operating income is mostly portfolio turnover rather than lease economics. Nine months to 2026-09-30: income from operations $79.3M, of which $55.4M — seventy per cent — is gain on sale of leased equipment, while total revenue rose 18% to $634.7M. Strip the gains and the operating business earned $23.9M in nine months against $94.6M of interest. The market's apparent requirement of only +6.6% growth is not a vote of confidence; it is what you get when the model divides operating cash flow by an enterprise value and never charges the company for the engines it buys. On the cash the business actually keeps, nine-month operating cash flow of $239.0M less net fleet investment of $419.6M is NEGATIVE $180.6M.
base_case_rationale: No number is recordable, for the fifth consecutive pass, and the reason is unchanged and verified again in this quarter's filing: two enormous input errors point in OPPOSITE directions and the schema can correct only one of them. FLEET CAPEX: `capex_series` is [$31.082M, $15.631M, $5.140M], the 'Purchase of property, equipment and furnishings' line, which the Q3 10-Q reports at $8,313k for nine months — sitting two lines below 'Purchase of equipment held for operating lease and for sale ( 837,574 )'. The extractor therefore reads office furniture and treats every engine as free, so the $347.6M base is operating cash flow less furniture. Net fleet investment has ACCELERATED: $419.6M for nine months against roughly $99M for the first half that the 2026-10-02 pass computed, i.e. about $560M annualised. SYNTHETIC COST OF DEBT: the model sets a 13.96% WACC on a lessor with $0.3M of goodwill, because EBIT of $104.3M over interest of $132.1M is 0.79x coverage and the synthetic rating reads distressed — while the rate Willis actually pays is $94,565k over $2,524,677k, about 5.0%, against a disclosed coupon stack of 3.10% to 8.00%. For an engine lessor sub-1x coverage is the business model, not distress. Applying the AROC pairing rule honestly: a sustaining base (annualised CFO of about $319M less maintenance capex of roughly $135M, being D&A of $121M plus $14M of equipment write-downs, plus the after-tax interest add-back) is about $279M paired with ZERO growth. At the engine's 13.96% WACC that prices the equity BELOW ZERO; at a defensible 7.0% — 72% debt at an after-tax 3.75% plus 28% equity at 11.5% — it prices the equity at roughly 2.7x the current price. The sign of the answer is set entirely by an input the schema cannot reach, so no final_growth is supplied.
key_risks: Gains on sale of leased equipment are $55.4M of $79.3M of nine-month income from operations — 70% of operating profit is portfolio turnover
Income from operations FELL 12.1% while revenue rose 18.3%, and income before taxes fell 34.3%; maintenance reserve revenue fell 22.2% to $141.3M
Nine-month operating cash flow of $239.0M against net fleet investment of $419.6M is negative $180.6M of owner cash flow, and the pace is accelerating
Revenue growth is increasingly low-margin parts trading: spare parts and equipment sales $141.0M at a ~14% gross margin against $120.6M of cost of sales
$2.52bn of debt plus a new Series B preferred at 8.09% sitting ahead of the common, on a fleet carried at values set in the tightest engine aftermarket on record
$13.0M of loss on debt extinguishment in nine months, and $165.8M of notes payable from failed sale-leasebacks on eight engines
watch_for: Gain on sale as a share of income from operations trending down — at 70% it is the single number that would expose the underlying lease economics
Maintenance reserve revenue: a second year of >20% decline would confirm the recurring line is eroding rather than timing out
Any disclosure splitting maintenance from growth fleet investment, still the one input that would make this name modellable
Whether net fleet investment stays near the ~$560M annualised run rate, and what incremental lease rent it produces
Selection-time gates on capex_series implausible against dep_amort_series and on the synthetic-versus-actual cost of debt — this name has now consumed five slots for five refusals
